owner: AKIEN owns this one outright. It is a change to the SEGMENT SHAPE he drew — whether the -2- edge stays one declared address or becomes several, and on what key — and no amount of measurement decides it. CC owns the measurement that provoked it and will own the code and proofs once he settles the shape.
watchme: none, because nothing is built yet to drift. The shape is a question, not a property that could regress; the instrument that would catch a regression (`./bin/cmd/feedbackmap`) already exists and already exits 0, and it would go red the moment a producer lost its route. A watch here would be a second mouth on a question `feedbackmap` already answers at every run.
intention: Settle whether a segment's -2- feedback edge carries ONE declared address, or several keyed by something — which side of the door a finding indicts, or who fired the segment.
why: MEASURED 2026-08-14 while declaring the route on all 17 finding-producers, and the whole reason to write it down is that the declaring is what found it — not a reading of the design. Akien's rule for the edge is verbatim: 'the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels.' — refined by him the same day, and the refinement is the frame this ticket sits in: 'really it shouldn't be number of steps it should be to the feedback target which is likely to be the previous step.' Applying it to real components, two populations came out where one address cannot tell the truth. FIRST (edge e): every chart-chain stage's inspector asks two KINDS of question — about the upstream berth it opened (upstream_berth_is_readable, request_identity_rides_the_chain, findings squarely about the previous stage's packet) and about the stage's OWN authored fields (every_constraint_carries_text_source_kind, the installed judges). The first kind has an upstream party; the second kind's author is the /chart ceiling, which is a hand, and a hand is not an address. One route serves the first and abandons the second. SECOND (edge f): learning_block and skill_block are handed their payload by a CALLER named in the call, not in the charter — and Akien's own design for learning blocks is 'learning blocks can send a task or whatever back if the inputs are not sufficient AT ALL STEPS' (2026-08-01), which IS a caller-returned route. A static field cannot spell it, so both declare themselves and say so. THE LIVED SYMPTOM this prevents, stated as a user would feel it: a finding arrives at a component that cannot act on it, so it is read, filed and dropped — and the segment reads GREEN on routing while nothing it could improve ever hears anything. That is the exact failure edge -2- was built to end, reappearing one layer in.
traces_to: Akien's segment drawing, 2026-08-14: machine -> inspector -1-> findings -> gate -> output -2-> feedback to [thing this thing feeds back to, might be the machine, might be anything else]. The bracket is his, and it is wide on purpose — this ticket asks how wide.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. 'one address is enough' was an assumption of the first build; declaring 17 routes measured it and it is false for two populations.

Law 9 — red is the default. feedbackmap now exits 0, and that green is honest about ROUTES DECLARED and silent about routes that land where nobody can act. This ticket is the distance from the spec that the green does not show.
cairn/tools/feedback filed edges (e) and (f), which are this ticket's two faces, and its earlier reservation of per-finding routing to Akien — all three are the same question.
gates: SHAPE FIRST, CODE SECOND, and BUILDME does not open until he has ruled. The options CC can see, offered as options and not as a recommendation: (1) keep one address and accept that self-indicting findings go nowhere, saying so in every charter — today's state, honest but lossy; (2) key the route by the finding's own subject (upstream vs own-output), which the record can already tell apart because the upstream-link entries are the guarded ones; (3) allow a route of 'the caller', resolved at firing time from the call rather than the charter, which makes route() need a caller argument and gives the two door components a real answer. Each is a different physics and (3) widens the tool's signature, which is why none of them gets prototyped first.
falsifier: RED if: (1) any option is built before he settles the shape — this is the ticket refusing its own eagerness; (2) a route resolved at firing time silently becomes a DEFAULT destination when the caller is unknown, which is the plausible-default failure NoRoute exists to refuse; (3) splitting the edge produces two mouths on one question — the charter saying one thing and a call site another, the defect that kept the route out of proved() in the first place; (4) the split is built for the chart chain alone and the two door components are left declaring themselves, which would be solving the half that was easy.
horizon: Whenever he next looks at the segment shape. NOT urgent: nothing delivers along the edge yet (cairn/tools/feedback edge (a) — the deliverer is unbuilt and grows against the first real finding), so no feedback is being misdelivered today. It becomes urgent the moment a deliverer exists, because then the wrong address is a real drop rather than a declaration.
dependencies: cairn/tools/feedback exists and is green at 18/18, so the population and the two failing kinds are measured rather than predicted.

The deliverer (feedback edge (a)) is NOT a dependency in either direction, but building it first would harden the one-address shape by giving it a consumer — which is an argument for settling this before that, not a blocker.
distinctions_recorded: THIS IS NOT 'the route should be computed instead of declared'. That question is already settled and settled the other way: a destination inferred from the failure is a guess wearing a measurement's clothes (feedback.py, and the three exchanges that produced it). Both edges here keep the declaration and ask what the declaration is allowed to SAY.

THE SELF-ROUTES ARE NOT ALL THE SAME. cairn/devices/tester routes to itself because persist_validation is the only hand that mints a trail link, so there is genuinely no upstream party — that one is a measured answer and this ticket does not touch it. learning_block and skill_block route to themselves because the upstream party cannot be SPELLED, which is the defect. A reader who lumps the three together will 'fix' one that is not broken.

THE QUESTION IS WHICH TARGET, NEVER HOW FAR. Akien retired the distance framing on 2026-08-14 — 'it shouldn't be number of steps, it should be to the feedback target' — so nothing here asks how many links to skip. orient proved the point in the same breath: he corrected its route to the TICKET, whose owner is a ticketing machine that does not exist yet, and that target is not N steps back from orient at all. It is simply outside the chain. A reader who arrives at this ticket looking for a hop rule has the wrong question.
provenance: Born 2026-08-14 out of the declaring itself. cairn/tools/feedback shipped that morning with filed edge (c) — '17 producers, 0 routed ... mass-producing 17 whys would be the fillable-field defect one level up' — and the whys were then written one at a time, each from a link measured in the component's own code. Writing them is what surfaced this: seven of the eight chart legs had an unambiguous upstream ref to point at, and the eighth (orient) had none at all, which is what made the two-kinds-of-question split visible. Edge (c) is closed on that charter; this ticket is what the closing measured.

chart_notes.orient: The two populations are named and countable, not sketched: eight chart-chain stages whose inspectors ask about both their input and their own output, and two door components (learning_block, skill_block) whose caller is a call argument. The refs are in the code — constrain.py:163, survey.py:165, decompose.py:144, triage.py:144, hypothesize.py:149, validate.py:152, verdict.py:109 — and orient.py has no upstream ref at all, which is the fact the whole split hangs on.
chart_notes.constrain: The bound is that this is HIS shape, not CC's to pick. It also inherits the bound already on the tool: a route is an address and nothing else, no urgency field, no mode, no enum ('we're leaving room for those, we're not building or ticketing those now') — so whatever splits, it splits by SUBJECT or by CALLER, never into a priority.
chart_notes.validate: The tooth a hollow build fails: take a real chart-stage record with one failing upstream-link entry AND one failing own-output entry, and require the routing to send them to different addresses. A hollow build passes by declaring two fields and sending both findings to the first one. The second tooth is the caller case — fire learning_block from two different callers with the same missing field and require the two findings to name different destinations; a hollow build returns the block's own address twice.

filed_edges: If the edge splits by subject, the split needs a rule for which subject an entry has, and the corpus already carries one implicitly: the upstream-link entries are exactly the guarded ones (appended only when the packet carries the ref). That is a code fact today and would become load-bearing, which means it would need to be stated in the grammar rather than inferred from control flow.

SEPARATE AND ALREADY FILED ELSEWHERE, so this ticket does not absorb it: three routes (orient, build_inspector, ruling) now name CairnCommons/tickets, an artifact store, while the owner Akien named — 'the ticketing machine would be the owner of that. and would get the feedback' — is unbuilt. That is cairn/tools/feedback edge (g), and it is a different question from this one: (g) asks whether a destination can ACT, this ticket asks whether one destination per segment is ENOUGH.
